correctness.rationale: Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2108.05174v1 gives a complete Banach lattice F=Fix(T_τ). For 0≤s≤τ, T_s|F and T_{τ−s}|F are mutual positive inverses and hence lattice automorphisms. For irrational a/τ, powers of T_a|F are norm-dense along the periodic group orbit, so the eigenspaces at exp(ijβa) equal ker(A−ijβI) for every integer j by strong continuity and differentiation at zero. The precise dimension inequality for a lattice homomorphism on Dedekind-complete F is verified in arXiv:1503.02430v2 Proposition 3.1(b), with the key independence lemma A.4 inspected. Handles β=0, all signed k, zero eigenspaces and finite/infinite dimension convention. An L1 two-speed translation example gives strict 1<2 multiplicity; no numerical data are required.

originality.rationale: The 2021 source explicitly identifies the semigroup geometric-multiplicity estimate as a plausible but unstated extension after Corollary 3.5. The 2015 result only treats a single bounded lattice homomorphism; applying it here requires a new exact eigenspace reduction using a periodic fixed lattice and an irrational sample. The inspected 2021 and 2025 semigroup papers establish spectral-set cyclicity or other operator-specific dimension bounds, not this uniform harmonic comparison. Published-record checks found no directly overlapping statements. Residual risk remains from an inaccessible classical monograph and unindexed equivalent formulations.

value.rationale: Theorem settles the concrete multiplicity refinement explicitly proposed immediately after Glück (2021), Corollary 3.5, rather than introducing an arbitrary invariant. In contrast to mere spectral cyclicity, it quantitatively constrains all finite eigenspace ranks without a pole or compactness hypothesis. An elementary but nonobvious periodic-fixed-lattice/irrational-sampling mechanism removes the resonance obstruction to applying discrete spectral theory. The strict two-speed L1 translation example demonstrates that the conclusion contains quantitative information absent from harmonic existence.
